name: Ukraine

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 579,400 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Low/high allow for the Natural Earth polygon vs official figure and inland water (surface area is a few % larger).

population.note: asOf 2025: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 38,980,376. World Bank total includes occupied territories and does not fully capture ~5-7 million refugees abroad; low 35 million. Population under Kyiv control is roughly 31-33 million (educated reading).

activePersonnel.note: CIA Factbook 2025: estimated 850,000-1 million active Defense Forces; Armed Forces of Ukraine infobox ~900,000 (2025); IISS as quoted (Wikipedia personnel list) 677,000 active (low, likely an earlier wartime count). Mid ~880,000. Excludes ~260,000 paramilitary (National Guard counted by IISS separately, though fighting at the front). asOf 2025-26.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Pre-war reserve (IISS 900,000) has largely been mobilized; remaining trained reserve is men with prior service not yet called. Very uncertain.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 880,000 minus infantry P roles (450,000). Covers navy and air force personnel, armour/artillery/air-defence crews, logistics, staff, training and other support.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to the observed war: ~1 million in uniform plus several hundred thousand casualties from ~33 million under government control (~4-5% already), with draft-age limits (25+) and exemptions limiting further call-ups.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized and assault brigade infantry at the front (~100+ brigades with chronic infantry shortages). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_Ukraine)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Western and Soviet mix, heavy drone integration.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Combat-hardened core but many short-trained mobilized men.

count.note: Educated guess. Territorial defence, airborne/air-assault, marine and rifle brigades. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_Ukraine)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical): Light weapons, FPV drones.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Mix of veterans and newly mobilized.

count.note: IISS 2024 rows on the equipment list: T-64 200+, T-80 80+, T-72 (multiple variants, captured), PT-91 26, Leopard 1A5 103, Leopard 2 ~60, Challenger 2 13, Abrams 22 among others. Wartime losses and captures make the 2026 holding very uncertain; mid ~1,000.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical): Mostly upgraded Soviet T-64/T-72; few Western tanks.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Combat-experienced crews.

count.note: IISS 2024 rows plus Western deliveries (Bradley ~300, CV90 ~50, Marder ~140, Stryker ~190, M113 ~700, BMP-1/2 several hundred, MRAPs). Mid ~3,500 after losses.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical): Mix of Western IFVs and Soviet BMP/BTR.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Combat-experienced.

count.note: Self-propelled and rocket systems sum to ~900 in the IISS 2024 rows (2S1, 2S3, 2S19, PzH 2000, Krab, M109, CAESAR, Bohdana, Zuzana, HIMARS, M270, BM-21) plus towed guns (D-30, M777, FH70, D-20). Bohdana production >10/month. Mid ~1,800.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Mixed; Western precision guns but shell-limited.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): The most combat-practised artillery arm in Europe.

count.note: IISS 2025 (p.202) as quoted: F-16 39 + MiG-29 45 + Su-27 23 + Mirage 2000 6 = 113 (inventory; serviceable fraction lower).

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical): Old Soviet fighters plus F-16AM/Mirage 2000-5.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Combat-experienced, thin pilot pool.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.25 (obsolete, a generation behind) (slightly above): Soviet-era, flying with Storm Shadow/JDAM-ER/glide bombs.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Combat-experienced.

count.note: Educated guess. Mi-8/17, Mi-24, Mi-2, plus donated Sea King/Westland types; wartime attrition, no reliable count on the fetched page. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Ukrainian_military_aircraft)

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Combat-experienced.

count.note: Educated guess. Group 2+ reconnaissance and strike UAVs (TB2 remnants, Shark, Leleka-100, Furia, Fury; long-range one-way attack drones and FPVs excluded per role rules). Massive drone war makes any count rough.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Innovative domestic designs, EW-hardened.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army): World-leading drone operators.

count.note: Educated guess. Navy lost most large ships 2014/2022; operates patrol boats, Island-class cutters, gunboats and naval drone (USV) units. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Navy)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly below): Small craft; Magura USVs excluded as munitions.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Combat-experienced.

count.note: S-300P/V ~170 launchers (~6 per battery, ~28), Buk ~50 launchers (~12), IRIS-T SLM 6 + SLS 7, NASAMS 14, Patriot 8, SAMP/T 1, Hawk 4+ batteries (IISS 2024/25 rows plus announced deliveries) = ~75 batteries.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Patriot/IRIS-T/NASAMS mixed with ageing S-300/Buk.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army): Most combat-practised GBAD force in the world.

count.note: Educated guess. Tochka-U remnants, Neptune, Flamingo/Ruta and Long Neptune launchers; ATACMS fired from HIMARS/M270 counted under artillery. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Armed_Forces_of_Ukraine)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Domestic cruise missiles emerging.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Combat use.

commandQuality.note: Rubric commandQuality 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders) (slightly below): Competent wartime staff with adaptation and drone-led innovation, but brigade-level coordination and rotation problems documented.

cohesion.note: Rubric cohesion 0.5 (national conscript army) (slightly above): National army in an existential war; strained by exhaustion, desertion (AWOL cases) and uneven rotation.

morale.note: Rubric morale 0.5 (average) (slightly above): Existential defence vs war fatigue after 4.5 years; range wide.

weapons.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Massed FPV and strike drones, glide bombs, Western precision munitions, domestic cruise missiles.

armor.note: Anchor 9: Soviet-era composite armour plus improvised cage/EW protection.

ships.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Naval USVs (Magura/Sea Baby) sank much of the Black Sea Fleet, but no major warships.

fortification.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Layered field fortifications and dense GBAD.

logistics.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Rail and road under constant strike; Western supply through Poland/Romania.

communications.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Starlink, Delta battle-management system.

isr.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Persistent drone ISR, Western intelligence sharing, commercial satellite imagery.

air.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: F-16/Mirage, no 5th generation.

cyber.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Experienced military cyber and HUR units.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 472,306,299,644 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD x 0.8005) / population 38,980,376 = 12,117. Range +/-20%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 590,014,115,733 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 472,306,299,644 2011 int$. Range +/-20% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Wartime: wider range for statistical gaps and damaged capacity. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: State at war: mid is the 2025 wartime share 39.56% of GDP (SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS; 33.96% in 2024); low is the last peacetime share 3.43% (2021). Excludes foreign military aid, which roughly matches domestic spending.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 17.9% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Large grain and oilseed exporter even in war (Black Sea corridor); output down vs 2021.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 18,137,513 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 6.224% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 225,779. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

drones.note: Educated guess. Group 2+ only (reconnaissance and strike UAVs); Ukraine claims millions of FPV drones a year, excluded. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Armed_Forces_of_Ukraine)

artillery.note: Educated guess. Bohdana 2S22 production reported >10 per month plus mortars.

missiles.note: Educated guess. Neptune/Flamingo launchers and ballistic programmes.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Domestic MRAP/APC (Kozak, Varta, Novator) and repairs.

armor.note: Educated guess. Tank overhaul rather than new production.

roadKm.note: As quoted: 169,694 km of which 166,095 paved (2012); occupied areas and war damage reduce the usable network (low).

railKm.note: asOf 2020: 21,626 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 3 large ports; low reflects Russian strikes and occupation (Odesa-Chornomorsk-Pivdennyi cluster still operating).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Not in the quoted UNCTAD table; CIA Factbook lists 410 Ukrainian-flag vessels (2023), mostly small river/coastal craft; many registered abroad. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_merchant_navy_capacity_by_country)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Defensive war on interior lines; supply runs by rail to ~50-100 km of the front, last mile under drone attack.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists only nine nuclear-armed states. Ukraine gave up its inherited Soviet arsenal under the 1994 Budapest Memorandum.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2-1.3: familiar terrain, fortified cities and lines, strong population support; depth west of the Dnipro and a harsh winter.

notes: Modern wartime snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle; ranges are deliberately wide because wartime holdings change monthly and official counts are secret. Population convention: World Bank total for everything inside ne:UKR including occupied areas; ne:UKR is the internationally recognised border, so Crimea and the occupied east are inside the polygon although Kyiv does not control them. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011; milSpendShare mid is the wartime share, low the last peacetime share (2021). Equipment from the Wikipedia equipment list quoting IISS Military Balance 2024 and 2025 rows; drones = Group 2+ only (FPV and long-range one-way attack drones excluded). Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). No major surface warships or submarines remain.
